I just purchased an ESP32. This is not an SBC, but a micro controller. It costs about $5, has no operating system and is programmable using the Arduino IDE. I like it because it has WiFi and idles in the micro amp range. It runs, with WiFi enabled in about 1 milliamps. This makes it suitable to run on a small battery. The processor can switch in and out of low power mode and running mode very easily. It has enough GPIO ports to be very useful, plus it has several integrated ADC/DACs so you don't need extra circuitry for analogue I/O. The CPU is 32 bits and runs many times faster than most Arduino systems.

Many companies sell developer boards with similar features. I'm excited to see what this can do. I expect to be able read sensors and control LED ropes using nano second timings with this baby.
